R070-01.notes: Reluctant start (pool, boredom) to hearing and adjusting beats herself. A: no business difficulties; C: no apology/conflict resolution; D: technique is only sketched, not step by step.

R070-02.notes: 'it' = imagining the pool summer; telling everyone = complaining openly. D contradicts nothing explicit but the text never says complaints stopped at once; B/C unsupported.

R070-03.notes: Wince 'as if someone had stepped on her foot' contrasted with 'To me it sounded like a piano.' A trap on literal pain; C unsupported since she simply goes to work.

R070-04.notes: Not wanting to be told what to expect parallels not explaining the beats ('She did not explain further') and letting the narrator discover them in the garage. A (routine sandwich) is the opposite disposition; B and D lack the parallel. Requires inference but only C supplies the same 'discover it without being told' logic.

R070-05.notes: 'I don't play... But I like to know it's ready' plus the late-wife context. B/C/D have no textual support.

R070-06.notes: Responds to the narrator's 'why so long on a piano no one played'; his listening counts as use. A is the literal-trap misreading; C/D unsupported.

R070-07.notes: 'for the first time I heard it' in the garage with fork and A key. A is explicitly contradicted ('I heard nothing but two notes'). Fork-vs-string beats slowing then vanishing as the pin brings the string to the fork's pitch is acoustically accurate; owning many forks but using one (typically A440) is realistic.

R070-08.notes: Simile depicts two nearly-matched frequencies producing a slow pulse. A is the tempting symbolic reading (narrator and aunt 'in step'), but 'equals' overstates and the sentence's function is describing the sound; B/D unsupported.

R070-09.notes: Pretending to read but no longer turning pages = attentive to narrator. B is a book-literal trap; C/D contradict the quiet approving tone.

R070-10.notes: Para 3 bored, watching the clock; para 6 striking, turning the pin, listening. Other options unsupported.

R070-11.notes: Glacial deposits at paleo-equator; magnetic-error and tilted-axis explanations 'won few converts.' A/C contradicted; D off-topic. Facts check: Budyko's late-1960s ice-albedo energy-balance model and his view that a frozen Earth could not recover are accurate; Kirschvink's 1992 short paper coined 'snowball Earth' and proposed volcanic CO2 buildup as the escape; Hoffman et al. 1998 Namibian cap carbonates atop glacial diamictites; ~700 Ma (Sturtian/Marinoan) and the high-obliquity alternative (Williams) are fair. No inaccuracies found.
